notes.plain: Rich mode behaves like the older workflow. It carries explanatory notes across the core branches so the map can stand on its own as both an outline and a lightweight narrative artifact.

This branch explains the intended release outcomes in enough detail that a collaborator can understand the product direction without reopening the original planning document. It includes the expected launch milestone and the usability target for new users.
The beta milestone should represent a coherent user slice with analytics, onboarding, and support readiness already wired in.
This goal focuses on shortening time to first success and removing confusing steps from the signup and activation path.
The risk branch is intentionally descriptive in rich mode so handoff readers can understand why each risk matters and what early warning signals should be watched during the launch window.
If design approvals slip, engineering and marketing assets both move, which compresses testing time and increases launch-day coordination load.
Missing event coverage would make it difficult to judge whether onboarding changes actually improved activation and would weaken the post-launch learning loop.
This branch records the sequence of key checkpoints, making dependencies between planning, review, and launch readiness visible to the whole team.
Draft plan review should lock scope, success metrics, and unresolved dependencies before implementation accelerates.
Launch review is the final gate for readiness, analytics confirmation, and fallback planning.
